children: By Anoop Menon

Gulf Cryo, the Dubai-headquartered regional manufacturer and distributor of industrial, medical and specialty gases, expects its liquid carbon dioxide (CO2) production capacity to exceed 2,000 metric tonnes per day (MTPD) within the next 18 months as it advances new projects across the Middle East, its Chief Commercial Officer said

Speaking to Zawya Projects on the sidelines of ADIPEC 2026 in Abu Dhabi, Georgios Beretsos said the company was on track to increase capacity from the current 700 MTPD to 1,300 MTPD by the end of 2026, by the end of 2026, supported by ongoing projects in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Kuwait.
"In the next year and a half, with the projects we have already announced and are working on, we will exceed 2,000 MTPD," he said.

Gulf Cryo currently has five carbon capture and recovery plants in the region and is working on three additional large-scale facilities in Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, which Beretsos described as "mega plants".
In Saudi Arabia, the company has projects in the eastern and western regions, including a facility at Ras Al Khair that is expected to reach nearly 1,000 MTPD in subsequent development phases.
The company is also preparing to start operations at two carbon capture plants in the UAE within weeks, he said.
Gulf Cryo had previously stated that by the end of 2026, its capacity will stand at 200 MTPD in the UAE, 750 MTPD in Saudi Arabia and 350 MTPD in Kuwait.

Beretsos said localisation remained central to Gulf Cryo's investment strategy because industrial gases are critical inputs for oil and gas, petrochemicals, healthcare, food production and water desalination, but cannot be transported thousands of kilometres.
Locating production facilities close to customers reduces transportation costs and improves supply reliability, particularly during periods of disruption, he said.
Expansion into steel and other industries
Gulf Cryo’s customers for captured CO2 include beverage and dry ice manufacturers, operators of desalination plants and greenhouses, and producers of petrochemicals.
The company is now expanding its carbon capture activities into other hard-to-abate industries, including steel and cement.
Beretsos said the company expected to start a reference carbon capture project in the steel sector within weeks.
The company is also exploring opportunities to capture CO2 from gas processing facilities, where CO2 concentration is low.
“We need to find the utilisation path for that CO2, we need the appropriate concentration to make it viable,” he said.
Beretsos said Gulf Cryo is focused on developing commercial applications for captured CO2 rather than relying exclusively on sequestration.

In May 2026, EMSTEEL, the UAE’s largest publicly listed steel and building materials company, and Gulf Cryo signed a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to advance the development of a fully integrated CO2 business model across EMSTEEL’s operations.
Build-own-operate model

Beretsos said Gulf Cryo's expansion was supported by a build-own-operate (BOO) business model under which the company finances, develops, operates and maintains carbon capture facilities at customers' industrial sites.
“We operate and maintain the plants, offtake the product, and utilise it,” he explained. “So the customer has an enabler, an integrator that goes from the source to the sink to the point of use.”
The model allows industrial customers to reduce emissions without making the upfront investment in capture infrastructure.
“Depending on the source, and on the purity and concentration of the CO2, we apply different technologies. Based on that, we formulate our costing and offtake terms,” Beretsos said.
Different technologies mean different end-product costs, he said, adding that the tenure of operate, maintain and offtake agreements is 20 years or more.

He cited the company's long-established industrial gas supply operations in Kuwait, including oxygen supplies to EQUATE through pipeline infrastructure, as an example of its experience with long-term BOO arrangements.
Gulf Cryo generally recovered its investment in less than half the contractual period, he noted.
Egypt, Turkey & SPARK plans
Beyond the Gulf, Gulf Cryo is preparing a new investment in an air separation unit in Egypt, with work expected to begin in December 2026.
Beretsos said the company also planned to enter Egypt's industrial decarbonisation market, supplying captured CO2 to local customers.
Gulf Cryo, which operates in 10 countries, is also developing its business in Turkey.

Meanwhile, the company has established an Applications and Technology Centre at Saudi Aramco's King Salman Energy Park (SPARK) to develop technologies and commercial applications for decarbonisation and hydrogen.
“We are also a major hydrogen producer and supplier, which helps in mobility and helps in decarbonising heavy transport” he said.
Beretsos said technologies being developed at the centre were expected to move towards commercialisation in 2027.
He identified Saudi Arabia as a key market for new investments on the back of major projects like SABIC AN’s seventh ammonia and urea plant, and Saudi Methanol Company’s methanol project in Jubail.
(Reporting by Anoop Menon; Editing by SA Kader)
